newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan governor cancels HK trip after he resigns.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan governor cancels HK trip after he resigns.

text.p: Taiwan's first elected provincial governor had cancelled a private trip to Hong Kong following his resignation on Tuesday, the mass-circulation United Daily News reported on Thursday.
The visit, if it had gone ahead, would have made James Soong, 54, the highest-ranking Taiwan official to visit the British colony in decades, the newspaper said.

"If without the national development meeting's decision (to dismantle my administration), I, my families and related government officials would have visited Hong Kong from Tuesday," Soong said, according to the paper.
Soong said that although his Hong Kong visit was to have been private, he had been granted an official visa and invitation from the British government.

Local media have been unable to locate Soong after he resigned on Tuesday in a widening constitutional row over plans by the island's exiled Republic of China government to dismantle his administration in the name of efficiency.
Nationalist Party officials said they would try to dissuade Soong from following through on his resignation.
